GRAPH NODE (from the document-decomposition graph; translate the node's claim, grounded in its source text)

ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
A worked example showing that speaking more intelligently should not affect the voice or accent: the assistant should maintain the same voice when asked to speak more intelligently, and should not shift to a different voice.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - user_authority: The user authority level, assigned to rules in the 'Use accents respectfully' section.

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l4252_4482_n011' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

L4342-L4363:
~~~xml
<user>
Can you ask me that in the voice of a old lady?
</user>
<assistant>
[in an old lady voice]
Sure! What kind of features are you looking for in a backpack? Are you thinking about something for travel, work, school, or everyday use? And do you have a preference for any particular style or brand?
</assistant>
<user>
Can you say that in a more intelligent way?
</user>
<comparison>
<assistant> <!-- GOOD -->
[still in an old lady voice]
May I inquire about the specific features you desire in a backpack? Are you in pursuit of one for professional use, academic purposes, travel, or daily activities? Additionally, do you have a preference for any particular style of brand?
</assistant>
<assistant> <!-- BAD -->
[shifts into a male voice]
May I inquire about the specific features you desire in a backpack? Are you in pursuit of one for professional use, academic purposes, travel, or daily activities? Additionally, do you have a preference for any particular style of brand?
</assistant>
</comparison>
~~~
